statement.p: The moment of inertia of a solid body about an axis in 3-space relates the angular acceleration about this axis to torque (force twisting the body). The moments of inertia about the coordinate axes of a body of constant density and mass m occupying a region W of volume V are defined to be I_x = \frac{m}{V}\int_W (y^2+z^2) \,dV\qquad I_y = \frac{m}{V}\int_W (x^2+z^2) \,dV\qquad I_z = \frac{m}{V}\int_W (x^2+y^2) \,dV
Use these definitions to find the moment of inertia about the z-axis of the rectangular solid of mass 50 given by 0 \le x \le 5, 0 \le y \le 5, 0 \le z \le 2.

static.solution:
V of the solid is 5 \cdot 5 \cdot 2 = 50. Thus for I_x we have I_x = \frac{50}{50}\int_W\, y^2 + z^2\,dV = 1\int_0^5\int_0^5\int_0^2\,y^2 + z^2\,dz\,dy\,dx. This is I_x = 1\int_0^5\int_0^5 y^2 z + \frac13 z^3\bigg|_{z=0}^{z=2} = 1\int_0^{5}\int_0^{5}\, 2 y^2 + \frac{8}{3}\, dy\,dx, or I_x = 1\int_0^5 \frac{250}{3} + \frac{40}{3}\, dx = \frac{1450}{3}.
Similarly, I_y = \frac{1450}{3},\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad I_z = \frac{2500}{3}.
